exitProficiencyTarget: Intermediate Low by ~grade 11, Intermediate Mid by grade 12 (Seal of Biliteracy threshold)
standardsBasis: Program-design target per expansion-plan-2026-09 §3 B1: WA credit crosswalk (RCW 28A.230.090 — Intermediate Mid = 4 credits) and Seal of Biliteracy (RCW 28A.300.575 — Intermediate Mid). Marketed against the Seal, not the Novice High graduation minimum. Standard tags use WA's 2015 World Languages standard numbers (5 Cs). Sub-standard numbering verified 2026-09-05 against the primary source (OSPI v1.3 PDF, p.6, "II. World Languages Learning Standards"): 1.1 Interpersonal/1.2 Interpretive/1.3 Presentational Communication; 2.1 Relating Cultural Practices/2.2 Relating Cultural Products to Perspectives; 3.1 Making Connections/3.2 Acquiring Information and Diverse Perspectives; 4.1 Language/4.2 Cultural Comparisons; 5.1 School and Global Communities/5.2 Lifelong Learning.
bandNotes: Intensive credit-track year: opens with a fast novice consolidation (weeks 1-4), then drives the Intermediate engine — past-tense narration (preterite/imperfect), future/conditional, subjunctive introduction, paragraph-length connected discourse, and spontaneous conversation on familiar and some unfamiliar topics. Authentic resources (news, poetry, short fiction, music) appear weekly from midyear. Weeks 34-36 rehearse AAPPL/STAMP-style tasks — the actual instruments WA names for banking credits and the Seal. Students entering without prior Spanish work the same weeks with heavier scaffolds; the placement diagnostic (plan §3 B2-B4) will route experienced students in at proficiency.

weeks.topic: Launch: proficiency goals & the Seal of Biliteracy
weeks.actflFocus: Communities: Lifelong Learning — setting a proficiency target and owning the path to it
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: What Intermediate means — hear Novice vs. Intermediate speech samples; map the ACTFL ladder.
Day 2: The Seal of Biliteracy and WA credit crosswalk — what Intermediate Mid unlocks (4 credits, transcript seal).
Day 3: Baseline self-assessment with can-do statements; rapid greetings/intro refresher.
Day 4: Speed-review carousel — numbers, questions, courtesy, survival phrases.
Day 5: Write and record your goal statement in Spanish; seal it for the year-end portfolio.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — discussing family origins and identity
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: The two-surname system — why many Spanish speakers carry both parents' apellidos.
Day 2: Interview frames — origins, languages at home, family story exchange.
Day 3: Read two short identity essays by bilingual teens; annotate key phrases.
Day 4: Draft your identity paragraph — raíces, languages, belonging.
Day 5: Identity round-table — share paragraphs, ask genuine follow-up questions.

weeks.topic: Daily life in the present tense (full system)
weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — describing your routines and habits in connected sentences
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Present-tense system consolidation — regular, stem-changing, reflexive, irregular yo-forms in one map.
Day 2: Soler + infinitive — talk about habits like a native ('Suelo madrugar').
Day 3: Compare weekday vs. weekend life with connector words (además, en cambio, por eso).
Day 4: Write a connected paragraph (not a list!) about your typical week.
Day 5: Speed-talks — 90 seconds on your daily life; peers note the connectors you used.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Reading — reading rich place descriptions
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Ser/estar/haber division of labor in place description; error-hunt exercises.
Day 2: Read travel-guide descriptions of Cartagena and Valparaíso; extract descriptive patterns.
Day 3: Neighborhood tour writing — describe your barrio with hay/está/es variety.
Day 4: Photo-prompt speaking — describe unseen-city photos to a partner who sketches them.
Day 5: Publish 'Guía de mi ciudad' entries; peer-read three and leave Spanish comments.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Practices to Perspectives — what family practices reveal about values
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: La sobremesa — the untranslatable hour after the meal; what it says about time and family.
Day 2: Family-values vocabulary through proverbs (dichos) about home and respeto.
Day 3: Interview task — ask a family member about their crianza; bring back one story.
Day 4: Discussion circles — which practices exist in your home? Which would you adopt?
Day 5: Reflective paragraph — 'En mi hogar, el valor más importante es...' with examples.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Products to Perspectives — dishes as history on a plate
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Dish map — mole, ceviche, empanadas, arepas: whose plate is whose?
Day 2: Read a real recipe in Spanish; command forms in instructions.
Day 3: Food history — how Indigenous, European, and African foodways merged.
Day 4: Write a recipe card for a family dish in Spanish, with steps in order.
Day 5: Cooking-show presentations — teach your dish to the class in Spanish.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — telling a completed travel story
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Preterite regular forms locked in; travel-story vocabulary.
Day 2: Model narrative study — a trip story's skeleton (arrival, highlight, mishap, return).
Day 3: Build your story outline (real or imagined trip) on that skeleton.
Day 4: Draft and peer-edit the narrative — 10+ sentences, sequenced.
Day 5: Story slams — tell your trip without reading; audience votes most inolvidable.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Reading — following event narratives with irregular past forms
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: The irregular preterite gang — fui/fue, hice/hizo, tuve, estuve, dije; pattern families.
Day 2: Read three short news-brief style event accounts; timeline each.
Day 3: Sequencing connectors workshop — entonces, en seguida, por fin, mientras tanto.
Day 4: Rewrite a bland account into a vivid one using connectors and irregulars.
Day 5: 'What happened?!' improv — draw an event card, narrate it convincingly in past tense.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — exchanging childhood memories
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Imperfect forms — the 'used to' tense; era, tenía, jugaba anchors.
Day 2: Childhood interview exchange — games, toys, fears, favorite places.
Day 3: Listen to adults recalling childhood (audio clips); note imperfect signals.
Day 4: Write 'Cuando era niño/a...' memory paragraph.
Day 5: Memory-swap circles; respond with follow-ups ('¿Y extrañas eso?').

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — weaving background and action into one story
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: The camera metaphor — imperfect sets the scene, preterite moves the action.
Day 2: Tense-choice drills on story sentences; justify every choice aloud.
Day 3: Picture-sequence narration — narrate a wordless comic with both tenses.
Day 4: Write an original mini-story (setting + event + desenlace).
Day 5: Story-telling festival — perform stories; audience identifies scene vs. action moments.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Practices to Perspectives — oral storytelling and what legends teach
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Read La Llorona (adapted) — track the preterite/imperfect texture.
Day 2: Legend jigsaw — El Dorado, la Pachamama, el cadejo; teams present.
Day 3: Why legends survive — fear, morals, place; discussion in Spanish.
Day 4: Draft your own short legend for a local landmark, past tenses required.
Day 5: Campfire-style telling (lights low); vote for best moraleja.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Reading — demonstrating comprehension of authentic-style texts across the fall's themes
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Rubric study + interpretive task — article and audio on family/travel themes.
Day 2: Interpersonal task — spontaneous paired conversation from a prompt envelope.
Day 3: Presentational task — narrate a past experience, recorded.
Day 4: Self-review recordings against the rubric; write a revision plan.
Day 5: Feedback conferences; log results in the proficiency portfolio.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — discussing habits and giving advice
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Wellness vocabulary; class habits survey (sleep, screens, exercise).
Day 2: Advice frames — deberías, te aconsejo que (subjunctive preview, unanalyzed).
Day 3: Read a teen-wellness article in Spanish; extract the top consejos.
Day 4: Peer advice exchange — describe a (school-appropriate) problem, receive counsel.
Day 5: Produce a bienestar tip-sheet for Spanish class students.

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Making Connections — health systems and medical literacy (health science link)
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Formal (usted) commands — tome, descanse, respire; where you'll hear them.
Day 2: Clinic dialogue practice — symptoms, questions, instructions.
Day 3: Read real-style medical instructions (dosage labels, appointment forms).
Day 4: Why medical interpreters matter — bilingual healthcare in Washington.
Day 5: Clinic simulation — patient intake to tratamiento, all in Spanish.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — presenting your plans with the future tense
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Future tense forms (hablaré, será) + ir a review; when speakers use each.
Day 2: Career vocabulary — match careers to school subjects and skills.
Day 3: Read about how Spanish proficiency boosts real WA careers (healthcare, trades, teaching, business).
Day 4: Draft 'Mi futuro' talk — studies, career, where you'll live, why.
Day 5: Deliver future-plans talks; peers ask one '¿por qué?' each.

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Making Connections — personal finance and work vocabulary (economics link)
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Work vocabulary + first-job talk; ahorrar vs. gastar habits discussion.
Day 2: Read simple job postings in Spanish; decode requirements.
Day 3: Build a one-page Spanish currículum (name, skills, experience).
Day 4: Job-interview role play with formal register (usted throughout).
Day 5: Budget challenge — allocate a part-time paycheck; defend your choices.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — negotiating hypotheticals politely

coreVocabulary.translation: in your place, if I were you

lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Conditional forms (haría, sería, podría) — softening and hypothesizing.
Day 2: Courtesy upgrade — '¿Podrías...?' '¿Te importaría...?' request ladders.
Day 3: Dilemma cards — 'What would you do?' small-group deliberations.
Day 4: 'En tu lugar, yo...' advice exchanges on realistic scenarios.
Day 5: Ethics fishbowl — one dilemma, structured whole-class discussion.

weeks.actflFocus: Communities: Lifelong Learning — measuring against the Intermediate bar at midyear
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Midyear IPA — interpretive set (article + audio) at Intermediate targets.
Day 2: Interpersonal task — sustained spontaneous conversation, 3+ minutes.
Day 3: Presentational task — past-and-future narrative, recorded and timed.
Day 4: Score, reflect, and compare against week 1 baseline recordings.
Day 5: Seal-of-Biliteracy planning conference — what STAMP/AAPPL asks, gap plan for spring.

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Making Connections — climate and sustainability (environmental science link)
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Environment vocabulary through an infographic on la Amazonía.
Day 2: Read a youth climate-activist profile from Latin America.
Day 3: Data talk — compare renewable-energy stats (Costa Rica, Uruguay, WA state).
Day 4: Draft solutions paragraphs — problems + deberíamos proposals.
Day 5: Mini climate summit — country teams present one commitment each.

weeks.actflFocus: Comparisons: Language Comparisons — a mood English barely has
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: What a 'mood' is — ojalá (from Arabic!) and the wish-world vs. fact-world.
Day 2: Present subjunctive formation from yo-forms; the opposite-vowel trick.
Day 3: Recommendation frames — 'Recomiendo que estudies...' advice carousel.
Day 4: Compare with English remnants ('I suggest he be on time') — why Spanish kept the mood alive.
Day 5: Ojalá poem — write six wishes for the world; read aloud.

weeks.actflFocus: Communities: School & Global Communities — Spanish in service of others
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Vocabulary through profiles of youth-led organizations in Latin America.
Day 2: Where Spanish helps locally — WA food banks, albergues, legal-aid clinics that need bilingual volunteers.
Day 3: Subjunctive in action — 'Es necesario que ayudemos...' cause statements.
Day 4: Design an awareness campaign for a chosen cause, materials in Spanish.
Day 5: Campaign pitches; class selects one to actually carry out this spring.

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Acquiring Information & Diverse Perspectives — migration told in migrants' own words
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: First-person migration narratives (adapted oral histories); listen and map each journey.
Day 2: Push and pull factors — discuss reasons in Spanish with evidence from the texts.
Day 3: La añoranza — poetry and song about missing home (e.g., a bolero or corrido excerpt).
Day 4: Washington connection — migration stories in our own community, handled with care.
Day 5: Reflective essay — 'Lo que aprendí de estas historias' with textual references.

weeks.actflFocus: Comparisons: Cultural Comparisons — bicultural life between two worlds
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Latino Washington — Yakima Valley, Seattle's South Park, eastside agriculture; population data.
Day 2: Bicultural voices — teens describe living between languages; el espanglish as identity.
Day 3: Compare celebrations — how holidays adapt across borders (posadas in WA).
Day 4: Local Latino businesses and festivals — research one and describe it in Spanish.
Day 5: Panel-style discussion — what does bicultural mean? Evidence from the week.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Products to Perspectives — murals as public voice
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Mexican muralism — Rivera, Orozco, Siqueiros; art meant for everyone.
Day 2: Frida Kahlo's autorretratos — describe and interpret one in Spanish.
Day 3: Symbol hunt — decode symbols in a mural; simboliza sentences.
Day 4: Design a class mural sketch expressing this year's learning.
Day 5: Gallery talk — present your mural section as a docent would.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Reading — reading and interpreting authentic poems
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Read a short accessible poem (Martí's Versos sencillos excerpt); sound before sense.
Day 2: Neruda's odes to ordinary things — how metaphor elevates a tomato.
Day 3: Mistral and modern voices; choose your favorite of the week's poems.
Day 4: Write an ode to an everyday object, Neruda-style.
Day 5: Poetry café — recite (memorized or read) with expression; snaps encouraged.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Products to Perspectives — film and song as cultural mirrors
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Watch a Spanish-language cortometraje (subtitles in Spanish); first-viewing reactions.
Day 2: Second viewing — analyze one scene's dialogue; subtitled vs. doblado debate.
Day 3: Song-lyric study — unpack one song's story and metaphors (recycles poetry tools).
Day 4: Write a review of the short film or song (opinion + evidence).
Day 5: Pitch a cortometraje idea — logline and opening scene in Spanish.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — comparing life experiences
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Present perfect (he comido, has viajado) — the 'ever/already' tense.
Day 2: '¿Alguna vez has...?' bingo — find classmates' surprising experiences.
Day 3: Challenge stories — un reto que has superado, told in pairs.
Day 4: Bucket-list writing — experiences you haven't had yet (todavía no he...).
Day 5: Two-truths-and-a-lie with present perfect; class interrogates in Spanish.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — defending opinions in structured debate
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Tech-and-society vocabulary through headlines; initial stance line-up.
Day 2: Opinion frames — creo que, en mi opinión, no estoy de acuerdo porque...
Day 3: Prep teams — screens in school: ¿ayudan o distraen? Gather arguments.
Day 4: Structured mini-debates with timed turns and rebuttals.
Day 5: Debrief + written position paragraph citing the strongest opposing point.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Reading — reading real news from Spanish-language outlets
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Anatomy of a Spanish news article — titular, lead, quotes; skim-reading strategies.
Day 2: Read one current article from a major Spanish-language outlet; summarize in 3 sentences.
Day 3: Compare coverage — same story in English and Spanish outlets; what differs?
Day 4: Interview practice — entrevista a classmate about a school 'news' event.
Day 5: Produce a class noticiero — anchor-desk news briefs, recorded.

weeks.topic: Country focus: Argentina & the Southern Cone
weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Practices to Perspectives — mate, asado, and shared time
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Southern Cone geography — Argentina, Chile, Uruguay; the pampas and Patagonia.
Day 2: El mate ritual — one gourd, one circle, strict etiquette; what sharing signals.
Day 3: Asado and sobremesa culture (recycles week 5); tango's story from port neighborhoods.
Day 4: Hear Argentine Spanish — the sh-sound of 'll' and vos conjugations in real audio.
Day 5: Costumbre exchange — present one Southern Cone custom and one of your own family's.

weeks.actflFocus: Comparisons: Language Comparisons — dialect variation as richness, not error
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: One language, many voices — hear the same sentence from Mexico, Cuba, Argentina, Spain.
Day 2: Word wars — popote/pajilla/sorbete: one straw, many names; regional word maps.
Day 3: Jerga sampler — teen slang from three countries (classroom-appropriate).
Day 4: English parallels — US/UK/Indian English varieties; why variation is normal.
Day 5: Dialect-detective challenge — identify audio clips by region using learned cues.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Reading — analyzing an authentic short story
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: First read of an adapted-authentic short story (e.g., a Cortázar or Quiroga selection); gist only.
Day 2: Close read — narrator, punto de vista, and where the story turns.
Day 3: Literature circles — roles (summarizer, word-hunter, questioner, connector).
Day 4: Analytical paragraph — claim about el tema, supported with a quoted line.
Day 5: Alternate-ending workshop — write and share a new desenlace in past tenses.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — building and delivering a persuasive case
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Anatomy of an argument — claim, evidence, concession, refutation; connector arsenal.
Day 2: Research day — teams build cases on assigned resolutions (in Spanish sources).
Day 3: Practice rounds with peer scoring on the rubric.
Day 4: Tournament day — formal debates with timed constructives and rebuttals.
Day 5: Judge feedback + written closing statement polishing por lo tanto conclusions.

weeks.actflFocus: Communities: Lifelong Learning — rehearsing the instruments that certify proficiency
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Test-format walkthrough — what AAPPL/STAMP tasks look like at each mode.
Day 2: Circumlocution bootcamp — describe words you don't know instead of freezing.
Day 3: Timed interpretive practice sets; strategy debrief after each.
Day 4: Simulated speaking tasks — picture prompts and voice recordings under time.
Day 5: Simulated writing tasks + strategy bank finalized; confidence check-in.

weeks.actflFocus: Communities: School & Global Communities — original research on Spanish in our region
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Choose capstone questions — Spanish in local schools, businesses, media, or family histories.
Day 2: Design instruments — encuestas or interview guides, drafted in Spanish.
Day 3: Collect data — surveys out, interviews conducted, sources logged.
Day 4: Analyze — organize hallazgos into claims with evidence.
Day 5: Build the presentation — visuals, structure, bibliografía complete.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — defending a year of growth at the Intermediate bar
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Capstone presentations, day one — research findings delivered entirely in Spanish.
Day 2: Capstone presentations, day two — Q&A defense from classmates and teacher.
Day 3: Portfolio assembly — week-1 goal recording vs. now; annotate the crecimiento.
Day 4: Exit conversation — one-on-one sustained interview at Intermediate targets.
Day 5: Despedida — certificates, Seal-of-Biliteracy next steps for juniors/seniors, and a proper hasta pronto.
